title: When the plan lock is switched on, a gym whose free trial ended long ago goes straight to read-only with no warning days
what: The plan lock gives a gym 7 grace days and then 30 basic days after its trial or paid time ends, and only then makes it read-only. It counts those days from the old end date, not from the day the lock is switched on. Gyms made before billing existed were told nothing locks when a trial ends. Any such gym whose trial ended more than 37 days before the switch is flipped wakes up read-only: no new members, nothing saved but looking and downloading, without ever seeing a grace or basic warning.
expected: Every gym that exists when the lock is switched on first gets the same warning days a new gym gets (grace, then basic), counted from the switch-on day, before anything closes.
who: owners of gyms whose trial ended before the lock went on
how_often: once, for every such gym, on the day the lock is switched on
fix_line: Count the warning days from the later of the trial end and the day the lock is switched on

title: Check-in numbers typed before the 3 Nov fix stay linked though the desk never checked them
what: Before 3 Nov anyone with the gym code could type a member's mobile at check-in and be linked to that member (plan, trainer, measurements, diet, workout plans). The fix makes a typed number wait for the desk. But links made the old way are left as they are: the desk has no list of them and is never asked to confirm them, so a wrong link made before the fix keeps seeing that member's details.
expected: Links made by a typed number before the fix are shown to the desk once to confirm or remove, the same way new typed numbers are.
who: gyms whose members checked in by typing a number before 3 Nov, and those members
fix_line: Put every link made by a typed number before the fix on the desk's confirm list

title: After an owner gives up a mobile number, whoever later gets that number can set a new PIN and run the gym
what: Forgot PIN sets a new PIN for every owner or staff login that has the mobile number a WhatsApp code was sent to. A person's mobile on the gym can never be changed, so an owner who moves to a new number keeps the old one on file. Indian operators give unused numbers to new customers after a few months. The new holder of that number can ask for a Forgot PIN code, set a PIN and sign in as the owner, with every member's name, phone and payments.
expected: A person can change the number they sign in with, and Forgot PIN on a login nobody has used for months asks for more than the WhatsApp code before it hands over the gym.
who: owners and staff who change their mobile number
how_often: rare: only after an old number is given to someone new
fix_line: Let people change their sign-in number, and add a second check to Forgot PIN for a login unused for months

title: A member the owner hid from the leaderboard shows on it again after leaving and coming back
what: The owner can hide a member from the gym leaderboard, for example for made-up workouts. The hidden mark is kept on the member's leaderboard row, and that row is deleted the moment the member leaves. When the member joins the gym again they are back on the leaderboard and in challenges, and the owner is not told.
expected: A member the owner hid stays hidden when they leave and rejoin, until the owner shows them again.
who: owners who hid a member, and the other members
how_often: each time a hidden member leaves and rejoins
fix_line: Keep the hidden mark for the gym's member, not on the leaderboard row that leaving deletes

title: Running an older server change file again quietly undoes later security fixes
what: Server changes are pasted into the live database by hand. Several files replace the same sign-in and create-gym steps one after another, and each file only warns in its header that running an older file again puts back its old version, so the next one must be run again after it. Nothing checks this. Running, for example, the PIN file again would take away the longer PIN lock and the one-trial-per-number check without any error.
expected: After every hand-applied change a check compares the live sign-in and create-gym steps with the newest files and says if any went back to an older version.
who: every gym, through MettleUp's own server work
how_often: only when an older file is run again by hand
fix_line: Add a check that the live versions of replaced steps match the newest file, run after each live change
